questions.title: How Overloads Differ
questions.description: Two methods in the same class are both named calc with exactly the same parameter list; one returns int and the other returns double. What happens?
questions.Option1: They form valid overloads and the int version runs
questions.Option2: They form valid overloads and the double version runs
questions.Option3: Compilation fails: methods cannot differ only by return type
questions.Option4: The program picks whichever method is defined first

questions.title: Overloading Binding Time
questions.description: The compiler selects which overloaded method to run using the argument types at compilation time. Method overloading is therefore an example of:
questions.Option1: compile-time (static) polymorphism
questions.Option2: runtime (dynamic) polymorphism
questions.Option3: no polymorphism at all
questions.Option4: runtime binding decided by the JVM

questions.title: Overload Resolution Order
questions.description: When one method call matches several overloaded versions, the compiler tries its resolution phases in a fixed order. Which order is correct?
questions.Option1: boxing, then exact match, then widening, then varargs
questions.Option2: exact match, then widening, then boxing, then varargs
questions.Option3: widening, then varargs, then exact match, then boxing
questions.Option4: varargs, then exact match, then boxing, then widening

questions.title: Meaning of Overriding
questions.description: A subclass overrides an inherited method when it defines a method with:
questions.Option1: the same name and the same parameter list
questions.Option2: the same name but a different parameter list
questions.Option3: a different name but the same parameters
questions.Option4: any name as long as the return type matches

questions.title: Final Methods and Overriding
questions.description: A method declared final in a superclass:
questions.Option1: must be overridden by every subclass
questions.Option2: can be overridden only with the @Override annotation
questions.Option3: cannot be overridden in any subclass

questions.title: Who Decides the Dispatch
questions.description: In dynamic method dispatch, the version of an overridden instance method that actually executes is chosen by:
questions.Option1: the declared type of the reference variable
questions.Option2: the actual class of the object at runtime
questions.Option3: the return type of the method
questions.Option4: the order in which the classes were compiled

questions.title: Override Annotation Purpose
questions.description: What does the @Override annotation do?
questions.Option1: Asks the compiler to verify the method really overrides a supertype method
questions.Option2: Makes the overridden method run faster at runtime
questions.Option3: Converts the method into a static method
questions.Option4: Hides the method from all subclasses

questions.title: Purpose of super.method()
questions.description: Inside an overriding method, the call super.describe(); does what?
questions.Option1: Calls the overriding method again recursively
questions.Option2: Creates a new object of the superclass
questions.Option3: Runs the superclass version of describe so extra work can be added around it
questions.Option4: Is only legal when describe is static

questions.title: Placement of super Calls
questions.description: Within an overriding method body, where may the statement super.compute(x); appear?
questions.Option1: Only as the very first statement of the method
questions.Option2: Anywhere among the statements of the method
questions.Option3: Only inside a constructor

questions.title: Covariant Return Meaning
questions.description: A covariant return type (allowed since Java 5) lets an overriding method return:
questions.Option1: Any unrelated class it likes
questions.Option2: A superclass of the original return type
questions.Option3: A primitive instead of a reference type
questions.Option4: A subclass of the original return type

questions.title: Widening Beats Boxing
questions.description: Demo overloads f with a long parameter and an Integer parameter. What does the main method print when it calls Demo.f(5)?
questions.Option1: Integer
questions.Option2: long
questions.Option3: Compilation error: the call is ambiguous

questions.title: Field Hiding vs Method Overriding
questions.description: B hides A's field and overrides A's method. What does the main method print?
questions.Option1: A followed by B.who
questions.Option2: B followed by B.who
questions.Option3: A followed by A.who

questions.title: Base Reference Dog Object
questions.description: A base type variable holds a subclass object. What does this program print?
questions.Option1: generic sound
questions.Option2: Compilation error: sound() cannot be called
questions.Option3: woof

questions.title: Super Call Then Subclass Line
questions.description: B's override calls super.hi() first and then prints its own line. What does this program print?
questions.Option1: A hi followed by B hi
questions.Option2: B hi followed by A hi
questions.Option3: B hi only

questions.title: Covariant Make Assignment
questions.description: Sub.make() overrides Base.make() with a covariant return type. What does this program print?
questions.Option1: base object
questions.Option2: sub object
questions.Option3: Compilation error: make() returns Base

questions.title: Static Binding Members
questions.description: Even when accessed through a base class reference, which members are always bound at compile time?
questions.Option1: Overridden public instance methods
questions.Option2: Abstract methods
questions.Option3: Static methods, private methods, final methods and fields
questions.Option4: Every instance method of the object

questions.title: Static Methods Hide Not Override
questions.description: B declares a static method with the same signature as A's static method. What does this program print?
questions.Option1: A static
questions.Option2: B static
questions.Option3: Compilation error: static methods cannot be called on a variable
questions.Option4: A static followed by B static

questions.title: Narrowing Visibility in Override
questions.description: Which rule governs the access modifier of an overriding method compared to the superclass method?
questions.Option1: It may be made more restrictive, e.g. public to private
questions.Option2: It may be widened, e.g. default to public, but never narrowed
questions.Option3: It may change freely in any direction
questions.Option4: It must always be exactly the same modifier as the superclass method

questions.title: Virtual Methods in Java
questions.description: Instance methods in Java are virtual by default. What does that guarantee?
questions.Option1: They are resolved using the reference variable's declared type
questions.Option2: They must be marked with a virtual keyword
questions.Option3: They cannot be overridden without interfaces
questions.Option4: The overridden implementation of the actual object runs, even through a base class reference

questions.title: Covariant Compile Check
questions.description: Dog.reproduce() overrides Animal.reproduce() with a covariant return type. Which statement about this program is true?
questions.Option1: It prints done
questions.Option2: Compilation fails at Dog d2 = new Animal().reproduce();
questions.Option3: A ClassCastException is thrown at runtime
questions.Option4: Compilation fails at Dog d1 = new Dog().reproduce();
